blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: We present CoTL, a framework that learns a compact set of tokens that preserves scene geometry and appearance from unposed multi-view images. Our encoder compresses the input images into small per-view sets of latent tokens that aggregate information across views to form a view-consistent scene representation. Each additional view expands the representation with only a small, resolution-independent set of tokens, allowing its capacity to grow with the available observations. To force this compact bottleneck to retain sufficient scene information, a query-based Gaussian decoder uses scene-independent queries to attend to the learned tokens and recover an explicit, renderable set of 3D Gaussian primitives. Novel-view rendering supervision trains the compact representation end to end through the reconstructed Gaussian scene. Experiments on \retenk{} and ACID show that the resulting compact, unstructured token set supports competitive novel-view synthesis and can serve as the latent space of a generative model for 3D Gaussian scene generation. Together, these results show that 3D Gaussian reconstruction is an effective objective for compact scene representation learning and the learned token space provides a basis for broader downstream tasks in 3D vision.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Learning a scene representation from multi-view images requires compressing view-dependent observations into a compact encoding of the underlying 3D world.
This representation must preserve shared geometry and appearance across views while discarding redundant view-specific information. Yet many recent feed-forward reconstruction models retain dense feature
representations produced by pretrained multi-view geometry backbones,
comprising hundreds of patch tokens per image.
A dominant class of feed-forward reconstruction methods uses dense pixel-aligned features as the visual memory,
predicting pixel-aligned Gaussian primitives from dense per-view feature grids [ 64 , 65 , 20 ] .
Other approaches decouple the Gaussian output budget from the input grid using clustered visual tokens,
global latent tokens, adaptive 3D anchors, or learned queries [ 46 , 18 , 17 , 35 , 1 , 28 ] . This indicates that the explicit scene output need not inherit the size and layout of the image grid, but the decoder still retrieves scene information from dense per-view patch features. A compact Gaussian output therefore does not imply a compact latent scene representation.

blocks.en:
Compact scene representations provide a practical interface for downstream models.
In 3D scene understanding, vision–language models often aggregate dense scene features into a compact set of tokens, enabling scene-level representations to be efficiently processed within the context budget of a language model [ 14 , 7 , 29 ] .
Compact representations are particularly useful for generation because they allow scene distributions to be modeled in a lower-dimensional latent space rather than directly over high-dimensional signals [ 37 ] .
Some existing 3D object-level generation models operate on 1D shape
tokens [ 66 , 74 ] , and recent work compresses
entire scenes into 1D tokens for generation or
reconstruction [ 56 , 2 , 8 ] .
In these methods, however, the tokens either encode geometry without
appearance [ 66 , 74 , 8 ] or are
decoded directly into target views without yielding an explicit, renderable
3D scene [ 56 , 2 ] . These designs leave open how
to learn a compact scene-level representation that jointly carries geometry
and appearance and can be decoded into an explicit, renderable 3D scene.

blocks.en:
In this work, we explicitly study compact scene representation learning from
unposed multi-view images. We present CoTL, a framework that places a
strict representation bottleneck between dense visual encoding and downstream tasks.
Given N N unposed images, our encoder represents each view with a small,
fixed set of latent tokens that aggregate information from its dense visual
features.
The resulting scene representation is view-scalable: its
capacity grows with the number of observations, while its per-view token
budget remains independent of image resolution.
These tokens are jointly contextualized across views to form
a compact, scene-dependent representation. Crucially, after this compression
stage, downstream prediction no longer accesses the original dense patch
features.

Since the contents of a latent scene representation are not specified by a direct
supervision target, we instead learn the representation by decoding it into an
explicit 3D Gaussian scene and supervising the rendered novel views. For this
objective to require the latent memory to carry the scene information needed
for reconstruction, the Gaussian decoder must receive no other input-dependent visual scene content
derived from the input. It therefore has no access to dense patch features, and its Gaussian queries are learned globally across scenes rather than initialized from image features or 3D anchors. The controlled
interface forces all scene-specific visual evidence through the latent memory,
while rendering supervision trains the memory to encode the information
required for novel-view reconstruction.

We evaluate the novel-view synthesis quality supported by the learned
representation across different numbers of context views and overlap
regimes on RealEstate10K [ 76 ] . Across the evaluated settings, the compact
representation supports competitive novel-view synthesis.
Experiments across view counts show that the representation incorporates
additional observations through a small, resolution-independent set of
tokens per view.
The RealEstate10K [ 76 ] -trained model also supports
novel-view synthesis on ACID [ 31 ] without fine-tuning,
providing evidence of zero-shot cross-dataset transfer. As a downstream
proof of concept, we train a flow-matching model in the learned token space
and decode its generated latents into explicit 3D Gaussian scenes using the
frozen Gaussian decoder. Together, these results show that
rendering-supervised 3D Gaussian reconstruction is an effective objective
for compact scene representation learning and that the resulting latent
space provides a basis for broader downstream tasks in 3D vision.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Scene representations can be learned from multi-view observations
through rendering supervision. [ 11 ] aggregates posed observations into a
fixed-size global scene representation and decodes it directly into the image at a
queried viewpoint. [ 25 ] similarly infers a
global scene latent from posed observations, but decodes it through a
conditional radiance field. Some
approaches [ 38 , 39 , 43 , 24 ] retain spatial features for each input view, so their
memory grows with both the number of views and the encoder feature-map
resolution. The encoder–decoder variant of
LVSM [ 21 ] instead compresses all observations into a fixed set of latent
tokens, and RayZer [ 19 ] extends this fixed-latent design to unposed
images. In such designs, additional observations must share the same latent budget. [ 55 ] condenses dense features
into ray-anchored tokens and allows the token budget to be selected at
inference. Although these approaches allocate
representational capacity differently, their decoders synthesize each
requested view from target-camera or ray queries, rather than first
decoding an explicit 3D scene.

A second group decouples Gaussian allocation from the input image grid.
Some methods use free learnable
queries [ 35 , 1 , 28 , 18 ] , while others
derive tokens by clustering visual features or construct them from
depth-based 3D anchors [ 46 , 17 , 72 ] .
These designs reduce or adapt the Gaussian output budget, but several
retain dense per-view features in the Gaussian-prediction path.
A compact Gaussian output therefore does not by itself
establish a compact latent scene representation. Our method instead
defines a compact, view-scalable scene memory at the encoder–decoder
interface, with a small, resolution-independent token allocation per
view, while its Gaussian output budget is controlled separately.
Rendering-supervised 3D Gaussian reconstruction provides the learning
objective for this memory, while its separation from the Gaussian
output makes it available as a latent interface for downstream 3D
tasks.

Our method learns a compact latent representation that summarizes
scene information across multiple unposed images. We learn this
representation through pose-free 3D Gaussian reconstruction, using novel-view
rendering supervision to optimize it end to end. Figure 2 summarizes the pipeline.

blocks.en:
The Gaussian decoder maps the compact scene memory 𝐒 \mathbf{S} to a set of 3D Gaussians 𝒢 \mathcal{G} via cross-attention.
Specifically, the decoder consists of a stack of Transformer layers initialized with M M scene-agnostic, learnable queries 𝐐 ∈ ℝ M × d \mathbf{Q}\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times d} .

Each layer performs cross-attention over 𝐒 \mathbf{S} and query
self-attention, followed by a feed-forward network.

blocks.en: 4.1.2 Training

We train our model on the official RealEstate10K training split [ 76 ] using four NVIDIA H100 GPUs with a per-GPU batch size of 6,
corresponding to a total batch size of 24.
Each training sample is constructed from a temporal window of a training video.
The first and last frames serve as the context endpoints,
additional context views are sampled from the intermediate frames,
and six of the remaining frames are used as rendering targets.
Training is performed at a resolution of 256 × 256 256\times 256 with a patch size of 16.
We express all camera poses and scene coordinates in a canonical frame anchored
at the first context camera and apply camera-distance normalization.
We use AdamW with β 1 = 0.9 \beta_{1}=0.9 and β 2 = 0.95 \beta_{2}=0.95 ,
together with a OneCycle learning-rate schedule.

We ablate the camera reference used to anchor the latent scene features.
We train three variants while keeping all other settings identical. In

features without a camera reference. In the global camera anchor variant, each view’s camera token is concatenated with its latent scene
features. In our pooled ray-map references variant, each latent scene

camera, as described in Sec. 3.2 .

the fraction of active Gaussians (opacity above 0.1) at the same

Our pooled ray-map construction provides a coarse coordinate reference from the start of training and mitigates this

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: In this work, we present CoTL, a framework for learning a compact, view-scalable scene representation directly from unposed multi-view images via 3D Gaussian reconstruction. By compressing multi-view inputs into a concise set of view-wise tokens, CoTL establishes an explicit information bottleneck: the scene memory serves as the sole condition for a set of scene-agnostic queries, forcing it to retain only the essential scene tokens required for high-fidelity geometric and appearance reconstruction.
blocks.zh: 在这部作品中,我们提出了COTL,一个学习紧凑,可视度可缩放的场景表现的框架,通过3D高斯重建直接取自无位多视图图像. 通过将多视图输入压缩为一组简明的取景符号,COTL确立了一个明确的信息瓶颈:场景内存是一组场景不可知性查询的唯一条件,迫使它只保留高真实度几何和外观重建所需的基本场景标志.

blocks.en: Furthermore, we demonstrate that this compact token representation provides an effective latent space for 3D generative modeling. Compared to video-diffusion-based scene synthesis, generating scene latents directly in this space significantly accelerates inference while enforcing strict cross-view geometric consistency. Once generated, the latent representation is decoded in a single feed-forward pass into an explicit 3D Gaussian scene, enabling real-time novel-view rendering without the per-view decoding overhead inherent to prior approaches.
blocks.zh: 此外,我们表明,这种紧凑的象征形式为三维基因模型的制作提供了有效的潜在空间。 相较于以视频扩散为基础的场景合成,在这个空间中直接生成场景潜伏物可以显著地加速推论,同时执行严格的交叉视图几何一致性. 一旦生成,潜伏的表示被解码成一个单一的向前传输的信号,传入一个清晰的3D高斯场景,从而可以在没有先前方法所固有的每景解码间接费用的情况下进行实时小说取景.

blocks.en:
Looking forward, we anticipate several promising directions.
Future work includes scaling up the pre-training data to explore whether this compact representation is able to generalize to open-world environments.
Additionally, we plan to extend the generative latent space to support flexible view counts and multi-modal controls ( e.g . , text conditioning). More broadly, we envision this compact scene memory acting as a general-purpose, reusable interface for downstream 3D understanding, interactive editing, and persistent spatial memory in embodied intelligence.
blocks.zh:
展望未来,我们期待若干有希望的方向。
今后的工作包括扩大培训前数据的规模,以探讨这种紧凑的表述是否能够通向开放世界的环境。
此外,我们计划扩大遗传性潜在空间,以支持灵活的取景计数和多式控制(例如文本条件)。 更广泛地说,我们设想这种紧凑的场景内存是一种通用的,可重复使用的接口,用于下游的3D理解,交互式编辑,以及所体现智能中的持续空间内存.

The complete model comprises the VGGT- Ω \Omega [ 48 ] encoder, a 12-layer Gaussian
